_about: Exercise library for the training app. Animation: each exercise has keyframes; every keyframe has the SAME number of elements in the SAME order (SVG viewBox 0 0 160 200). Interpolate polyline points and circle centers linearly between consecutive keyframes; draw in array order. 'raw' elements are static SVG snippets. If 'scale' is set, wrap the drawing in transform translate(80*(1-s),185*(1-s)) scale(s). 'ground' = draw a line from (6,186) to (154,186) stroke #CBD2CD width 2. timingMs = [toFinish, holdFinish, toStart, holdStart]; phase s goes 0->1 with cosine easing (0.5-0.5cos(pi*u)), holds, then 1->0, holds, loop. With k keyframes, s maps across them: pos=s*(k-1).

sessions.name: Strength A
sessions.blurb: Full body: hinge, push, single leg, rotation, pull and core.
sessions.warmup: 10-min golf mobility routine, then 1–2 light sets before the first lift.
sessions.footer: Save time by pairing 3 + 4 and 5 + 6 as supersets. Week 1: 2 sets of everything at a weight you could lift about 12 times.

exercises.name: Trap bar deadlift
exercises.why: Total-body strength and the ground force that powers your swing.
cues: Stand in the middle of the bar, handles in line with the middle of your feet.
Hips back, chest proud, flat back. Pull the slack out of the bar before it leaves the floor.
Push the floor away and stand tall. Squeeze your glutes at the top; don't lean back.
exercises.avoid: Rounding the lower back or yanking the bar off the floor.

animation.alt: Hinged at the hips gripping trap bar handles, back flat → Standing tall holding the trap bar at arm's length

exercises.name: Dumbbell bench press
exercises.why: Upper-body pushing strength that's easier on the shoulders than a barbell.
cues: Feet flat on the floor, shoulder blades squeezed together and down.
Lower with elbows about 45° from your sides until the dumbbells reach chest level.
Press up and slightly in. Stop just short of locking your elbows.
exercises.avoid: Elbows flared straight out to the sides.

animation.alt: Lying on a bench, dumbbells lowered to chest level → Lying on a bench, dumbbells pressed straight up over the chest

exercises.name: Split squat
exercises.why: Single-leg strength and hip stability that protect your knees when running.
cues: Take a long stance so the front shin stays close to vertical at the bottom.
Drop straight down, back knee toward the floor.
Drive up through the whole front foot, torso tall.
exercises.avoid: Front knee caving inward.

animation.alt: Standing in a split stance holding dumbbells at the sides → Lowered into a split squat, back knee near the floor

exercises.name: Half-kneeling cable chop
exercises.why: Trains controlled rotation through the upper back, the same turn as your downswing.
cues: Set the cable high. Kneel side-on to it with the inside knee down.
Pull the handle diagonally from high to low across your body.
Keep your hips square. The turn comes from your ribs and shoulders.
exercises.avoid: Twisting the hips or leaning to finish the rep.

animation.alt: Front view, kneeling, both hands reaching up to a high cable on the left → Front view, kneeling, hands pulled low across the body to the right

exercises.name: Single-arm dumbbell row
exercises.why: Upper-back strength and better posture over the ball.
cues: Knee and hand on the bench, back flat, neck neutral.
Pull your elbow up and back toward your hip.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly to a full stretch.
exercises.avoid: Twisting the torso to heave the weight up.

animation.alt: One knee and hand on a bench, back flat, dumbbell hanging at arm's length → Elbow pulled up and back, dumbbell beside the ribs

exercises.name: Pallof press
exercises.why: Teaches your core to resist rotation, which protects your lower back.
cues: Stand side-on to a chest-height cable, feet hip-width.
Press the handle straight out from your chest and hold for 2 seconds.
Don't let the cable pull you around. Ribs down, hips square.
exercises.avoid: Rotating toward the cable as your arms extend.

animation.alt: Top view, standing side-on to a cable, hands at the chest → Top view, arms pressed straight out from the chest while resisting the cable

exercises.name: Standing calf raise
exercises.why: Calf and Achilles durability for running.
cues: Balls of your feet on the edge of a step. Hold a rail for balance.
Rise as high as you can onto your toes and pause for 1 second.
Lower for 3 seconds until your heels drop below the step.
exercises.avoid: Bouncing through the bottom of the rep.

animation.alt: Standing on a step edge with heels lowered below it → Raised high onto the toes on the step edge

sessions.name: Strength B
sessions.blurb: Full body: squat, pull, hinge, press, lateral, power and carry.
sessions.warmup: 10-min golf mobility routine, then 1–2 light sets before the first lift.
sessions.footer: Save time by pairing 3 + 4 and 5 + 6 as supersets. Throw the med ball fresh: rest fully between sets.

exercises.name: Goblet squat
exercises.why: Squat strength, plus ankle and hip mobility under load.
cues: Hold one dumbbell vertically against your chest, elbows tucked.
Sit down between your heels with knees tracking over your toes.
Drive up through the whole foot, chest tall.
exercises.avoid: Heels lifting or knees caving inward.

animation.alt: Standing tall holding a dumbbell at the chest → Deep squat with the dumbbell at the chest and chest up

exercises.name: Lat pulldown
exercises.why: Your lats drive the downswing, and pulling balances all the pushing.
cues: Grip slightly wider than your shoulders, thighs snug under the pad.
Lean back slightly and pull the bar to your upper chest, elbows down and back.
Let the bar rise under control to a full stretch.
exercises.avoid: Swinging your torso or pulling the bar behind your neck.

animation.alt: Seated at a pulldown machine, arms reaching up to the bar → Bar pulled down to the upper chest, elbows driven down

exercises.name: Romanian deadlift
exercises.why: Hamstring and glute strength, and the hip-hinge pattern behind every good lift.
cues: Soft knees. Push your hips back as the dumbbells slide down the front of your legs.
Keep a flat back and lower to just below the knees, or until your hamstrings stretch.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall.
exercises.avoid: Rounding your back or turning it into a squat.

animation.alt: Standing holding dumbbells in front of the thighs → Hips pushed back, torso hinged forward, dumbbells below the knees

exercises.name: Half-kneeling landmine press
exercises.why: A shoulder-friendly press that also trains your core to stay braced.
cues: Kneel with the knee down on the same side as your pressing arm.
Brace your core and squeeze the glute of the down leg.
Press up and forward until your arm is long. Don't lean back.
exercises.avoid: Arching your lower back to finish the press.

animation.alt: Half-kneeling, holding the end of a landmine bar at the shoulder → Half-kneeling, arm pressed up and forward

exercises.name: Lateral lunge
exercises.why: Side-to-side hip strength and adductor mobility for a stable swing.
cues: Take a wide stance with your toes pointing forward.
Sit your hips back over one leg. Keep the other leg straight, foot flat.
Push off the bent leg to return to center.
exercises.avoid: The bent knee caving inward.

animation.alt: Front view, standing in a wide stance → Front view, hips sitting over the bent right leg, left leg straight

exercises.name: Rotational med ball toss
exercises.why: Teaches fast hip-to-shoulder rotation, the power source of your swing.
cues: Stand side-on to a wall, a few feet away.
Load into your back hip with the ball by your back pocket.
Turn your hips first, then your torso, and throw hard into the wall.
exercises.avoid: Throwing with your arms only.

animation.alt: Front view, rotated away from the wall with the ball low by the back hip → Front view, turned toward the wall, arms extended, ball released

exercises.name: Suitcase carry
exercises.why: Grip strength, obliques and posture, all in one walk.
cues: Hold a heavy dumbbell in one hand and stand tall.
Walk slowly with short steps, shoulders level.
Don't lean toward or away from the weight.
exercises.avoid: Leaning to one side.

animation.alt: Walking tall with a heavy dumbbell in one hand → Mid-stride on the other foot, dumbbell steady at the side

sessions.name: Golf mobility
sessions.tag: Before every lift + Wed & Fri · 10 min
sessions.blurb: Hip rotation, upper-back rotation, shoulders and ankles: the areas your swing relies on.
sessions.warmup: Before a round: do 2, 4, 5 and 8, then 10 easy half swings.
sessions.footer: Every 4 weeks: sit with a club across your chest and turn each way, hips still. More turn with no strain means it's working.

exercises.name: Cat-cow
exercises.why: Wakes up the whole spine before you load it.
cues: Hands under shoulders, knees under hips.
Exhale: round your back up toward the ceiling and tuck your chin.
Inhale: let your belly drop and lift your chest and gaze.
exercises.avoid: Rushing. Move slowly and breathe with each rep.

animation.alt: On all fours with the back rounded up → On all fours with the back arched and chest lifted

exercises.name: Quadruped thoracic rotation
exercises.why: Builds the upper-back turn that powers a full backswing without straining your lower back.
cues: On all fours, put one hand behind your head.
Thread that elbow down toward your support wrist.
Rotate the elbow up toward the ceiling, following it with your eyes. Hips stay still.
exercises.avoid: Shifting your hips or twisting from the lower back.

animation.alt: On all fours, hand behind head, elbow pointing down to the floor → On all fours, elbow rotated up toward the ceiling

exercises.name: Open books
exercises.why: Opens up chest and upper-back rotation for a bigger shoulder turn.
cues: Lie on your side, hips and knees bent 90°, knees stacked, arms straight out in front.
Sweep your top arm up and over to the other side, eyes following your hand.
Keep your knees together and on the floor.
exercises.avoid: Knees lifting apart as you rotate.

animation.alt: Lying on the side seen from the head end, both arms stacked in front → Top arm swept open to the floor behind, chest facing up

exercises.name: 90/90 hip switches
exercises.why: Trains hip internal and external rotation, both of which your swing needs.
cues: Sit with both knees bent 90°, one leg in front, one out to the side.
Keep your feet planted and rotate both knees over to the other side.
Sit tall. Use your hands behind you for support at first.
exercises.avoid: Slumping or rounding your back.

animation.alt: Top view, seated with both knees pointing to the left → Top view, seated with both knees rotated to the right

exercises.name: World's greatest stretch
exercises.why: Hips, hamstrings and upper-back rotation in a single move.
cues: Step into a long lunge with both hands on the floor inside your front foot.
Drop your inside elbow down toward the instep.
Then rotate that arm up to the ceiling, eyes following your hand.
exercises.avoid: Letting the back knee collapse. Keep the back leg long.

animation.alt: Long lunge with hands on the floor, inside elbow dropped toward the front foot → Long lunge with one hand down and the other arm reaching to the ceiling

exercises.name: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch
exercises.why: Loosens hips that tighten from sitting, freeing up hip rotation and your running stride.
cues: Kneel on one knee with the front foot flat.
Squeeze the glute of the down leg and tuck your pelvis under.
Shift your hips forward until you feel the front of the hip stretch. Stay tall.
exercises.avoid: Arching your lower back instead of moving your hips.

animation.alt: Half-kneeling, upright → Half-kneeling with the hips shifted forward and the back hip stretched

exercises.name: Knee-to-wall ankle mobility
exercises.why: Ankle mobility helps your squat depth, running stride and a stable lower body in the swing.
cues: Face a wall with your front toes a few inches from it.
Drive your knee forward to touch the wall, keeping the heel down.
Once it's easy, move the foot back a little. Aim for 4–5 inches.
exercises.avoid: Letting the heel lift off the floor.

animation.alt: Split stance facing a wall, front knee straight → Front knee driven forward to touch the wall, heel down

<rect x="140" y="10" width="10" height="176" rx="2" fill="#E4E8E5" stroke="#6B7770" stroke-width="2"></rect>

exercises.name: Band pull-aparts
exercises.why: Wakes up your upper back and shoulders and improves your posture at address.
cues: Hold a light band at shoulder height, arms straight out in front.
Pull the band apart until your arms form a T, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Return slowly. No shrugging.
exercises.avoid: Shrugging your shoulders up toward your ears.

animation.alt: Top view, arms straight out in front holding a band → Top view, arms pulled out wide in a T

exercises.name: Bodyweight squat to stand
exercises.why: Grooves a deep, comfortable squat and stretches your hamstrings.
cues: Feet shoulder-width. Sink into a deep squat holding your shins or toes, chest up.
Keep holding and lift your hips to straighten your legs into a forward fold.
Let go, stand tall and reach your arms overhead.
exercises.avoid: Forcing depth. Only go as low as is comfortable.

animation.alt: Deep squat holding the shins with the chest up → Standing tall with arms reaching overhead
